text:
maria: Opening a follow-up thread from the postmortem — recurring GPU surge last Thu. Summary: autoscaler lag + low headroom caused Dedicated pools to throttle. Need remediation ownership, timelines, and recurring checks.

devon: thanks — can we list concrete action items here and owners?

maria: yes. high-level items I have:
- quota request (increase soft limit for dedicated-pool-us-west) -> owner: kai, ETA: 2 business days
- scheduler tuning (max-sched-retries, backoff) -> owner: sree, ETA: 1 week
- headroom policy (maintain X% free GPUs per region) -> owner: jamie, ETA: 3 days to propose, 2 sprints to implement
- monitoring/alerts (surge pattern detector on queue depth + burn rate) -> owner: devon, ETA: 4 days

kai: can take quota request. Filed JIRA-942. Request payload sent to infra-portal, awaiting quota team approval. ETA realistic: 48 hours if no follow-ups.
sree: I'll own scheduler tuning. First step: reproduce surge in staging, capture scheduler logs. Putting config patch on a branch: `gitlab.com/rw/runtime/scheduler#gpu-tuning-1930`.
maria: please also include a canary plan for the scheduler change (small region, low-traffic tenant).
sree: good call. Canary plan: 10% traffic US-WEST for 48h, fallback to current config on error.
jamie: I'll draft headroom policy. Proposal: keep 12% headroom for peak 99th percentile workloads, dynamic buffer during deploy windows. Will post doc link by EOD.
devon: monitoring — I'll add a composite alert: if queue_depth > 300 and node_util > 92% for 10m then page eng-sre + ops. Also dashboard with rolling 1h/6h burn-rate.
ops-bot: Incident report: <https://incidents.internal/r/GPUSurge-2026-03-20|GPUSurge-2026-03-20> created by incident-bot.
maria: timeline check: want initial proposals in by Fri COB. Owners, ackable?
kai: ack — JIRA-942 linked, will update PR when quota portal responds.
sree: ack — starting reproduction now.
jamie: ack, posting draft in #eng-runtime by 2026-03-24.
devon: ack, alert runbook draft will be in the repo under `runbooks/gpu_surge.md`.
maria: also flag recurring incident pattern: similar surge happened 3 times in last 8 weeks around 10:30-11:00 PST on Tues/Thu — hypothesis: batch job overlap + customer A ramp. Action: add scheduled capacity scavenger and coordinate with customers.
sree: can we get a simple CSV of job start times? I'll run a query against scheduler logs and attach.
devon: query I used: `SELECT start_time, tenant, gpu_count FROM job_events WHERE start_time >= now() - interval '60 days' AND gpu_count > 16;` result will be in the incident doc.
maria: escalate any blockers to me. We'll have a 30m sync Thu 09:00 PT to review progress. Invite list: maria, devon, sree, kai, jamie, capacity-oncall.
kai: pinging quota team lead @quota-svc — appreciate fast track if possible.
jamie: quick note: if headroom policy is approved, we should include cost estimate (monthly delta) in the doc. I'll add a spreadsheet.
devon: adding a post-checklist: regression tests, canary metrics, rollback playbook snippet. Example snippet for rollback:```kubectl apply -f scheduler-config-prev.yaml```
maria: thanks all. I'll convert this thread into a follow-up checklist in the postmortem doc and assign owners there (tracking fields: owner, jira, eta, status). Please update JIRA or the doc when status changes. :thumbsup:

sree: small question — should scheduler tuning be gated until quota is approved?
maria: no, proceed in parallel but block wide rollout on quota success. Canary can run without quota if we limit tenants.
sree: got it.

kai: update 1930130656 — quota portal approved soft limit increase, pushed to prod request, ETA for capacity: ~24h.
maria: perfect, once capacity available we'll sequence canary + headroom enforcement. Closing thread when all action items are in status: blocked/in-progress/done in the postmortem doc.
